assessment_note: The selected instrument is MSCA-PF, a unit-cost instrument. Per the CLAUDE.md C1 constitutional amendment (§8.1, §8.4, §7 Phase 7), which ranks above this skill specification, the budget gate for a unit-cost instrument is satisfied by the internal deterministic derivation (unit_cost_budget.json), not by a lump-sum external response in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/. Consequently, the lump-sum received/ channel is not the applicable budget source for this instrument, and its absence is NOT a blocking gate failure: Constraint 4 (absent response is a blocking failure) governs lump-sum responses for lump-sum instruments only. Response-conformance validation was performed against the applicable budget source. The unit-cost derivation is present and complete: its gate_pass_declaration is 'pass', all four line items are resolved to Confirmed, unresolved_components is empty, blocking_inconsistencies is empty, and the derivation is byte-equal replay-checked (a deterministic derivation, not an estimate). Structural coverage was confirmed against Phase 3 wp_structure.json: all five work packages (WP1-WP5) and all four partner identifiers (DATA_PARTNER, HOST, TRANSFER_PARTNER, VALIDATION_PARTNER) are covered by the whole-duration unit-cost derivation. An MSCA-PF single-researcher action is budgeted for the whole action rather than partitioned per work package or per partner, so the absence of per-WP and per-partner budget lines is expected and is not an inconsistency. No numeric budget value (cost, currency amount, or effort/month count) has been materialised, computed, copied, quoted, or written to this artifact — only structural field references are recorded (Constraint 1 enforced). The categorical Phase-8 block (§8.4) is preserved and instrument-independent; it is satisfied here because every budget component resolves to Confirmed. No blocking inconsistencies are unresolved; the budget gate passes.
